govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FBISecrecy_FBI_: George Lardner Jr.’s FBI Exempt From Order on Secrets covers the secrecy ruling. The Bureau kept its secrets. Lardner covered the intelligence beat. The ruling favored the Bureau. The file belongs to the political archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
problems-in-american-democracy: Thames Williamson's civics text guided high-school students through the workings — and the challenges — of American democracy. Voting, parties, courts, and current issues of the day are explained with the aim of making informed citizens. A window into what young Americans were taught about their government a century ago.
temporal-power-a-study-in-supremacy: Marie Corelli, the best-selling dreamer of her day, pictures a ruler clothed in strange, holy power in this high romance. Her heady brew of faith and melodrama held millions spellbound. Grand, odd, and true-hearted Corelli from first page to last.
the-prospective-mother-a-handbook-for-wo: Dr. J. Morris Slemons wrote this plain-spoken handbook to guide women through pregnancy — month by month, with advice on health, diet, and care. Meant for mothers with no doctor at hand, it offered calm, practical counsel. A revealing look at how childbirth was managed a century ago.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alexandre-de-: This 1913 reference article on the Marquis de Tracy — Louis XIV's viceroy in New France. Lionel Lindsay tells his stern rule. He humbled the Iroquois threat. Quebec's colony grew under him. The Sun King's man in Canada. His regiment built the first Quebec forts.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-anne-first-du: This 1913 reference piece on the Duke of Montmorency — Anne, Constable of France. Georges Goyau tells his long career. He served four Valois kings. Dreux's field ended his life. The sword of the old monarchy. His chateau crowns the Chantilly woods.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-annecy: This 1913 reference article on Annecy — the Savoyard diocese of St. Francis de Sales. Georges Goyau gives its story. The lake mirrors its old town. Geneva's loss was Annecy's gain. The saint's beloved city. Its palace floats on the canal. Its bishops guard the saint's relics.
